rulings.challenge_claim: The row discloses the weaker of two available byte-parallels, states a difference at the site it does disclose that the bytes do not carry, ships the recurrence claim untiered, and leaves unnamed a source block whose reuse begins and ends at exactly this row's two seams.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on all three arms, re-derived from the bytes. (1) The disclosed relation is overstated. The row's closing splice at oshb:Jer.50.43 and the corresponding idiom at oshb:Jer.49.24 are four words each; re-collated word by word they share exactly one byte-identical form, כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה (the anguish noun differs in accent, צָרָה֙ against צָרָ֧ה). The seizing verbs are different roots inside the idiom, הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְהוּ against אֲחָזַ֖תָּה; oshb:Jer.49.24 inserts a further noun, וַחֲבָלִ֛ים; and it carries no counterpart to חִ֖יל (that form is absent from oshb:Jer.49.24 at consonantal tier: 0 tokens). (2) The stated difference is not the difference the bytes carry. The device note names the difference as the verb of onset, glossing it against “Damascus has grown feeble,” (web:Jer.49.24); those are the two verses' opening verbs, standing outside the four-word idiom the note is about, and the feebleness predicate in fact stands inside oshb:Jer.50.43 as well (וְרָפ֣וּ יָדָ֑יו). The note's 'near match' also ships with no tier. (3) The byte-nearest relation is unnamed. This span reproduces oshb:Jer.6.22-Jer.6.24: oshb:Jer.50.42 and oshb:Jer.6.23 are 19 words each and share 16 byte-identical word forms; the three divergences are the substitution of בַּת בָּבֶֽל for בַּת צִיּֽוֹן, the pronoun הֵ֨מָּה֙ for הוּא֙, and a live mater pair, defective וְכִידֹ֞ן against plene וְכִיד֞וֹן. oshb:Jer.50.43's closing idiom differs from oshb:Jer.6.24's only in the verb's pronominal suffix (הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְהוּ against הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְנוּ), and oshb:Jer.50.41 opens with the same three words as the corresponding clause inside oshb:Jer.6.22, הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א, byte-identical at both - the two verses sharing 5 byte-identical word forms of 50:41's 11, and differing in the north phrase and in 50:41's added plural-kings clause. That reuse begins and ends at this row's own two seams, so disclosing it would have corroborated the cut; naming a one-form parallel in its place inverts the evidence weight. The cut itself stands and is not disturbed: both row splices re-collate at byte tier at their cited refs, and the tier-1 scene-shift onset at 50:41 is unaffected.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the near-match sentence with what the bytes carry, tiered - inside the four-word idiom the two sites share one byte-identical form only, the seizing verbs are different roots, Jer.49.24 adds a noun and lacks the writhing noun. device_notes: add the source-block relation with its digits and tiers - Jer.50.42 shares 16 of its 19 word forms with Jer.6.23 at byte tier (divergences: the Babylon-for-Zion substitution, the pronoun, and the defective-against-plene spear noun, a live mater pair), Jer.50.43's closing idiom differs from Jer.6.24's in the verb's pronominal suffix alone, and the reuse begins and ends at this unit's own two seams, corroborating the cut. boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Jer.6.22, web:Jer.6.23, web:Jer.6.24, oshb:Jer.6.23, oshb:Jer.6.24. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field if a reuse driver is added. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every recurrence sentence carries a collate tier and a digit naming the swept object and its unit; the stated difference is re-collated inside the quoted extent at both refs and matches what the bytes carry there; every verse argued in prose outside this unit's span stands in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: First challenge: the setumah cited to close the unit at 50:46 carries no single-witness disclosure, unlike the other mark citations in this stretch. Second challenge: the grammatical test used to reject a cut at 50:44|50:45 is byte-false, the block relation that would actually carry the rejection is unstated, a setumah after the parallel lion verse is undisclosed counter-pressure, and the closing mark citation drops both its witness prefix and its single-witness qualifier.
rulings.grounds: Both upheld. The two challenges are the SAME defect on the mark citation and DISTINCT on everything else. (a) Mark citation - one defect, converged: the mark is correctly typed (the single-witness inventory records a setumah at MT 50:46), but the closing sentence cites it bare, with no witness prefix on an MT-keyed layer and no single-witness qualifier, and the evidence list carries the plain ref without the disclosure tag this same tiling uses at 51:14, 51:19 and 51:24. (b) The rejection warrant is byte-false, and this arm is the more serious. oshb:Jer.50.44 ends לְפָנָֽי, completing its rhetorical question at the verse end, and oshb:Jer.50.45 opens לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ, a fresh therefore-imperative clause; both witnesses break there. No sentence runs across that boundary, so the test said to kill the split never runs. (c) The warrant that would carry the rejection is unstated and verifies: oshb:Jer.50.44 and oshb:Jer.49.19 share 23 byte-identical word forms of 50:44's 28, and oshb:Jer.50.45 and oshb:Jer.49.20 share 20 of 24, so the first two verses travel as one reprise block. The third does not: oshb:Jer.50.46 and oshb:Jer.49.21 share exactly one byte-identical word form (הָאָ֑רֶץ), so calling all three verses one reprise overstates the third. (d) The undisclosed counter-pressure verifies: the single-witness inventory records a setumah at MT 49:19, immediately after the parallel lion verse - tier-3, weak, corroboration only, never a driver, and absence would prove nothing either way, but it is span-relevant pressure toward a division the row rejects without naming it. Verified sound and not disturbed: the ketiv/qere handling at oshb:Jer.50.44 is byte-exact, one note in the single-witness inventory, the source carrying both forms inside the verse, with the plural object suffix אֲרִיצֵם֙ standing against the singular אֲרִיצֶ֨נּוּ at the Edom site; all three row splices re-collate at byte tier at their cited refs.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the grammatical-continuation test and replace it with the block warrant that carries the rejection - Jer.50.44-45 travel with Jer.49.19-20 at 23 of 28 and 20 of 24 byte-identical word forms, so the pair reads as one reprise - and add the second sentence the rival disclosure earns: the third verse shares one word form with Jer.49.21, and a setumah stands at oshb:Jer.49.19 (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only) where the parallel sequence divides. boundary_rationale: cite the closing mark as oshb:Jer.50.46 with the setumah type and the single-witness qualifier, matching the disclosure form used at the neighbouring marks, and drop the bare witness-less ref. boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.49.20 and web:Jer.49.20, web:Jer.49.21 for the verses argued in prose. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the replacement warrant must survive the test that killed the original - read the verse-end and verse-onset bytes at 50:44|50:45 and show the warrant does not depend on a sentence running across them; every parashah citation in the row carries witness prefix, claimed type and single-witness qualifier, checked as a sweep over every mark key falling in or adjacent to the span, not as a spot fix.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere at 51:3, in the very verse the row argues from; the English attached to the 51:5 splice runs past what the splice contains; and the row's Hebrew engagement stops short of the cipher name its onset claim sits on.
rulings.grounds: Refined: two arms hold, the third does not, so the framing overstates. HOLDS - the disclosure omission. The single-witness inventory records one ketiv/qere note at MT 51:3, inside this span, and the doubling is visible in the verse bytes themselves, the verb standing twice, once pointed and once bare: יִדְרֹ֤ךְ ידרך הַדֹּרֵךְ֙. The row argues from that verse's content and says nothing about the note, while the notes at 51:9 and 51:13 are disclosed where they fall in the adjacent units; in the book's 141-note, 124-verse inventory a span-touching note is an unconditional disclosure, and the asymmetry sits inside one stretch. HOLDS - gloss extent. The splice at oshb:Jer.51.5 covers the phrase the English renders “For Israel is not forsaken,” (web:Jer.51.5), while the clause attached to it runs on through “nor Judah, by his God,” (web:Jer.51.5), which renders וִֽיהוּדָה֙ מֵֽאֱלֹהָ֔יו - words the splice does not contain. DOES NOT HOLD - the cipher-name arm. The onset claim rests on the divine-speech formula, which the row does quote and which re-collates at byte tier verse-initially at oshb:Jer.51.1; no rule obliges engaging a name the row makes no claim about, so leaving לֵ֣ב קָמָ֑י unengaged is a missed opportunity, not a defect. Verified sound and not disturbed: the frame-ownership reasoning stands - the chapter's four divine-speech onsets (sweep at consonantal tier: 4 verses in this chapter - 51:1, 51:33, 51:36, 51:58 - of 152 book-wide) are all narratorial, with no human mouth carrying the formula in this span - and treating the 50:46|51:1 boundary as a unit seam inside a parent that continues is correct. The paseq seg recorded at MT 51:2 is a count-only layer and its non-disclosure is not part of the defect.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.51.3 - one note, single-witness inventory - and splice the doubled reading from the source bytes rather than describing it, matching the disclosure form this tiling uses at 51:9 and 51:13. boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.51.3 (ketiv/qere). boundary_rationale: re-cut the 51:5 pairing so gloss extent equals splice extent - either shorten the English to the clause the splice covers or extend the splice through the following two words. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: run the span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry as a sweep over every ketiv/qere, parashah and special-letter key falling inside Jer.51.1-Jer.51.5 before postcheck, not as a spot fix at 51:3 alone; and re-collate each splice against the exact clause it is glossed with.

rulings.challenge_claim: The two-speaker reading inside 51:9-10 is carried by the English punctuation rather than by anything the Hebrew marks; the note claim quotes no Hebrew form and sources its position to an inventory that supplies only a count; and the English attached to the 51:6 splice runs past what the splice contains.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on all three arms. (1) The mouth change is not byte-marked. oshb:Jer.51.9 and oshb:Jer.51.10 run continuously in the first person plural with no speech frame between them - five first-person-plural forms across the two verses: רִפִּ֣ינוּ and וְנֵלֵ֖ךְ at 51:9, צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ, וּנְסַפְּרָ֣ה and אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ at 51:10 - and the source marks no change of speaker. What separates the row's foreign voice from its returning exiles is the nested single quotation the English rendering opens at web:Jer.51.10 and not at web:Jer.51.9: modern punctuation, tier-4, never evidence in either direction, and never counterevidence by absence either. (2) The note claim is mis-sourced. The claim that the note falls on the verse's opening verb is credited to the inventory, which records a count for that verse and nothing else; the position and the variant are readable only in the verse bytes, where the doubled reading stands verse-initially, רפאנו רִפִּ֣ינוּ, and the row supplies no splice at all for a Hebrew form claim. (3) Gloss extent. The splice at oshb:Jer.51.6 covers the phrase the English renders “Flee out of the middle of Babylon!” (web:Jer.51.6), while the clause attached to it runs on through “Everyone save his own life!” (web:Jer.51.6), which renders וּמַלְּטוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ. Verified sound and not disturbed: the splice re-collates at byte tier, 51:6 is a genuine verse-initial imperative onset, and refusing to treat the embedded voice as a fresh frame-owner is the right call under this book's formula-ownership hazard; the seam stands and the defects are characterisation and citation hygiene.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: drop the two-mouth distinction between 51:9 and 51:10 or re-ground it. State what the bytes carry - one continuous first-person-plural voice across the two verses, spliced, with no speech frame between them - and if the distinction is kept, name its source as the English rendering's nested quotation and disclaim it as tier-4, never evidence. device_notes: splice the doubled reading at oshb:Jer.51.9 from the source bytes, attribute its position to the verse bytes, and keep the inventory citation to what the inventory records - one note, single-witness. boundary_rationale: re-cut the 51:6 pairing to the splice extent, or extend the splice through the escape clause. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every speaker or mouth claim in the row names a byte-marked speech frame or is disclosed as tier-4 English punctuation; every inventory citation claims only what the inventory records, with position read from verse bytes; every splice re-collates against the exact clause it is glossed with.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated seam driver does not separate this cut from two uncut imperative clusters in the same stretch; a byte-true stirring-verb thread crossing three adjacent unit onsets goes undisclosed; the English attached to the 51:11 splice runs past what the splice contains; and a comparison to a denser note cluster later in the chapter carries no verse and no digit.
rulings.grounds: Refined: the driver arm and both lesser arms hold; the stirring-thread arm does not establish a defect. HOLDS - the driver does not discriminate its own seam. Discourse-imperative onset as stated fits oshb:Jer.51.8, which carries הֵילִ֣ילוּ עָלֶ֗יהָ קְח֤וּ, and oshb:Jer.51.12, which carries שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס, equally well; neither is cut. What separates 51:6 and 51:11 from those two is verse-initial position - both cut onsets stand at word 0 of their verses, both uncut clusters stand mid-verse - and the row never names it. HOLDS - gloss extent. The splice at oshb:Jer.51.11 covers the phrase the English renders “Make the arrows sharp!” (web:Jer.51.11), while the clause attached to it runs on through “Hold the shields firmly!” (web:Jer.51.11), which renders מִלְא֣וּ הַשְּׁלָטִים֒. HOLDS - the unanchored comparison. The device note sets this verse's single note against a denser cluster later in the chapter with no verse and no digit; cross-unit references are verse-anchored, and the site is MT 51:34 at five notes. DOES NOT HOLD as framed - the stirring thread. The root is byte-present at all four sites named (מֵעִיר֩ at oshb:Jer.50.9, יֵעֹ֖רוּ at oshb:Jer.50.41, מֵעִ֣יר at oshb:Jer.51.1, הֵעִ֣יר at oshb:Jer.51.11), but it recurs AT successive onsets rather than straddling any one seam, so it corroborates the cuts instead of arguing continuity against them; it is a texture object, never row evidence by itself, and no sourceable digit exists for it, since the unpointed skeleton of the root collides with the noun for city and a bare substring sweep would be a blended count - which the challenge concedes. Verified sound and not disturbed: both splices re-collate at byte tier, the setumah at MT 51:14 is correctly typed and single-witness disclosed, the ketiv/qere at MT 51:13 is correctly counted at one, and the seam itself stands.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: name the discriminator the seam actually uses - a verse-initial discourse imperative - and say that the mid-verse imperative clusters at 51:8 and 51:12 do not open units under this reading. boundary_rationale: re-cut the 51:11 pairing to the splice extent, or extend the splice through the shields clause. device_notes: verse-anchor the comparison - oshb:Jer.51.34, five notes, single-witness inventory - instead of naming a cluster later in the chapter. Do NOT add the stirring-verb thread as a boundary claim: if it is disclosed at all it belongs in device_notes as texture, with the swept object named per attested form and no root-level digit, since the unpointed skeleton collides with the noun for city. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: applied mechanically across this stretch, the stated driver must select this seam and reject 51:8 and 51:12; every cross-unit reference carries a verse and a digit naming its object; every gloss matches its splice extent on re-collation.

rulings.challenge_claim: First challenge: all three original-language citations pair a Hebrew splice with a curly-quoted WEB clause taken from elsewhere in the same verse, and the closing sentence uses a positional row reference rather than a verse-anchored one. Second challenge: the same three mispairings, plus a doxology-twin claim shipped untiered against a text that diverges in three of its five verse pairs while the row sits at high confidence with no frontier flag.
rulings.grounds: Both upheld. The three mispairings are the SAME defect in both challenges; the register arm and the untiered-twin arm are DISTINCT additions. (1) Gloss extent fails three times of three, and the mispairing runs in both directions rather than one consistent offset. At oshb:Jer.51.15 the splice covers עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ, the phrase the English renders “He has made the earth by his power.” (web:Jer.51.15), while the clause attached is “He has established the world by his wisdom.” (web:Jer.51.15), which renders מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ. At oshb:Jer.51.16 the splice covers לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ, rendered “When he utters his voice,” (web:Jer.51.16), while the clause attached is “there is a roar of waters in the heavens,” (web:Jer.51.16), which renders הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֨יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם - precisely the words the row's own at-the-sound argument says are NOT the phrase in question, so the mispairing undercuts the argument it is placed under. At oshb:Jer.51.19 the splice covers the verse-final יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ, rendered “Yahweh of Armies is his name.” (web:Jer.51.19), while the clause attached is “The portion of Jacob is not like these,” (web:Jer.51.19), which renders the verse-opening לֹֽא כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲק֗וֹב. Each English string is itself verbatim; the failure is the pairing. (2) The twin claim is untiered and the bytes do not sustain it whole. Re-collated verse against verse, oshb:Jer.51.15 reaches byte tier at oshb:Jer.10.12 and oshb:Jer.51.18 byte tier at oshb:Jer.10.15, but oshb:Jer.51.16, oshb:Jer.51.17 and oshb:Jer.51.19 all reach tier none against oshb:Jer.10.13, oshb:Jer.10.14 and oshb:Jer.10.16 - two of five pairs byte-identical, three divergent. Two of those divergences are live mater pairs the row owes: plene יַעֲק֗וֹב at 51:19 against defective יַעֲקֹ֗ב at 10:16, and defective צֹרֵ֖ף at 51:17 against plene צוֹרֵ֖ף at 10:14; 10:16 also carries וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל, which 51:19 does not. A unit that names the relation, sits at high confidence and carries no frontier flag owes those divergences a tier and a disclosure. (3) The closing sentence anchors the following material by its position in the tiling rather than by verse. Verified sound and not disturbed: all three splices re-collate at byte tier at their own refs, the false lamed-header call at 51:16 is correct, the genre shift from second-person judgment address to third-person hymn is byte-marked, and the setumah marks bracketing the unit at MT 51:14 and MT 51:19 are correctly typed and single-witness disclosed. The boundary is not disturbed; the evidence base under it is.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut all three Hebrew-to-English pairings so gloss extent equals splice extent at 51:15, 51:16 and 51:19; at 51:16 the pairing must carry the at-the-sound phrase the row's own argument turns on, not the clause that follows it. boundary_rationale or device_notes: tier the twin claim per verse pair and disclose the divergences - byte tier at 51:15 against 10:12 and 51:18 against 10:15, tier none at 51:16, 51:17 and 51:19 against 10:13, 10:14 and 10:16 - naming the two live mater pairs (plene Jacob at 51:19 against defective at 10:16; defective goldsmith at 51:17 against plene at 10:14) and the extra name word standing in 10:16. confidence and frontier_flag_considered are dependent fields of that correction and must be re-opened against the corrected evidence base. boundary_rationale: replace the positional reference to the following unit with a verse-anchored one. boundary_evidence_refs: add the per-verse refs actually argued (oshb:Jer.10.13, oshb:Jer.10.14, oshb:Jer.10.15, oshb:Jer.10.16) beside the range. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: each splice re-collates against the exact WEB clause it is glossed with, at the cited ref; the recurrence claim carries a per-pair collate tier rather than a bare relation label; and no positional unit reference survives the register sweep of the row's prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: First challenge: the closing citation pairs the Hebrew splice for the verse-final formula with a curly-quoted WEB clause drawn from earlier in the same verse. Second challenge: the same mispairing, plus a break-in-pieces refrain digit that is false under both units, plus an English gloss at 51:20 running past its splice.
rulings.grounds: Refined: the defects are real and the severity stands, but the second challenge's supporting book-wide digit is itself object-blended. The two challenges are the SAME defect on the closing mispairing and DISTINCT on the digit and the 51:20 overrun. (1) The refrain digit is false, as charged. The form spliced here from oshb:Jer.51.21, וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔, stands 9 times across Jer.51.20-Jer.51.23, distributed one, two, three, three, the instances varying in accent (sweep at consonantal tier: 4 verses, 9 token occurrences), so the row's fivefold is wrong under the token reading and wrong under the in-span verse reading, and it names no unit and carries no sweep citation. (2) CORRECTION to the challenge: its parenthetical calls 5 the book-wide verse count of that form and lists 13:14 among the sites. It is not. The 5-verse digit belongs to a sweep of the bare verb alone, וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י (spliced from oshb:Jer.51.21), which matches as a consonantal substring inside וְנִפַּצְתִּים֩ at oshb:Jer.13.14 - a different form, with a different suffix and no second word - exactly the substring class this book's sweep hazards name. The refrain form itself sweeps at consonantal tier to 4 verses book-wide, all four inside this row's own span; there is no out-of-span site. (3) Gloss pairing fails at the close: the splice at oshb:Jer.51.24 covers the verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה, rendered “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.51.24), while the clause attached is “all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight,” (web:Jer.51.24), which renders אֵ֧ת כָּל רָעָתָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂ֥וּ בְצִיּ֖וֹן לְעֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם, the clause immediately before it. (4) The gloss on the splice at oshb:Jer.51.20 likewise runs past it, to cover כְּלֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה. A further citation-hygiene point neither challenge names: the closing sentence's subject is the divine-utterance formula, but its ref carries the parashah tag, so a mark disclosure is attached to a formula claim. Verified sound and not disturbed: both splices re-collate at byte tier, the addressee shift at oshb:Jer.51.20 is marked in the pointed bytes by second-masculine forms against the second-feminine address at oshb:Jer.51.13, the setumah at MT 51:24 is correctly typed and disclosed, and reading the postpositive formula as closure corroboration is right, since a fresh onset does follow.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the bare fivefold refrain with the swept object, unit, scope and digit - the two-word form spliced from the bytes, standing 9 times across Jer.51.20-Jer.51.23 (sweep: 4 verses, 9 token occurrences), all four verses inside this unit's span. Do NOT carry a bare-verb digit: that sweep matches inside a longer form at 13:14 and is a blended count. boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing pairing so the verse-final formula splice is glossed with the clause that renders it, and re-cut the 51:20 gloss to the splice extent or extend the splice through the weapons clause. device_notes: separate the two objects in the closing sentence - the mark citation keeps the setumah type and the single-witness qualifier, the closure claim cites the verse bytes for the formula. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every digit names its object (attested form, not root), its unit (verses or tokens) and its scope (in-span or book-wide), and is not sourced from a sweep that matches inside a longer form; every splice re-collates against the exact clause it is glossed with.

rulings.challenge_claim: First challenge: the cross-seam catchword citation misidentifies the bigram that actually recurs between the two mobilization calls, and the 51:27 pairing quotes a shorter Hebrew span than the English beside it. Second challenge: the quoted pair does not stand in the verse it is attributed to, its digit belongs to an object the row never names, the stated ground for refusing a seam at 51:27 tests only for parent-level header shapes while a neighbouring unit is allowed to open on the very class denied here, and the row's remaining bounding warrant is a tier-3 mark pair while the byte-grade closure at the preceding verse goes unnamed.
rulings.grounds: Both upheld; the catchword arm is the SAME defect in both challenges, and the warrant arms are DISTINCT additions. (1) The citation is byte-false at the site it is attributed to. The pair בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ, carried under a byte-tier label and placed against the call standing at web:Jer.51.27, re-collates at tier NONE against oshb:Jer.51.27; it reaches byte tier only at oshb:Jer.51.12, and there the first word is the nomen rectum of the phrase governing the imperative, אֶל חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס, so the pair splices across a phrase boundary and is not a call at either site (sweep at consonantal tier of that pair: 1 verse, oshb:Jer.51.12 alone). (2) The digit belongs to an unnamed object. The form the two verses actually share is שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס at 51:12 against שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס at 51:27 - the same two words, differing in the accent on the second, so the recurrence holds at accent_stripped tier across the pair and not at byte tier. That form sweeps at consonantal tier to 4 verses book-wide (4:6, 50:2, 51:12, 51:27), 2 of them in this chapter: the chapter digit the row cites fits an object it neither names nor quotes.
